two_point_forces — DRIVE pegtactile op

• Data kinds: table × signal × signal × signal × signal × signal → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.two_point_forces(kp, F, M_g, g, tip, axis, mu_grid=None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import pegtactile; pegtactile.two_point_forces(kp, F, M_g, g, tip, axis, mu_grid=None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("two_point_forces"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Decomposes the wrench of a two-point contact (Whitney) into 2 contact forces and the wall friction μ (planar; Coulomb assumption with both points sliding downward).

In the tilt plane (horizontal component e of the axis), the tip edge touches the wall on the −e side (normal = horizontal, friction = upward), and the body touches the edge of the narrowest part on the +e side (normal = perpendicular to the axis, friction = upward along the axis). For each μ, (f_n1, f_n2) is the least-squares solution of 3 equations (F_e, F_z, M), and the μ with minimum residual is refined with a parabola (default grid 0 to 1.5, 301 points). Returns mu / fn_tip / fn_mouth / resid (N) / p_tip / p_mouth. Raises ValueError: axis too vertical for the tilt plane to be determined, vectors that are not 3 finite components, μ grid with fewer than 3 points.
